note: Corps of Engineers park on a wooded point of Truman Lake west of Warsaw, in two loops 500 m apart: Loop A on a timbered peninsula (30 A sites plus five without electric), its far end about 45 m from the shore through the trees, and Loop B (50 A with water) on the ridge away from the lake. Swimming beach, boat ramp and playground; a separate group camp. --Claude
summary: rec.gov read (USACE's own pages refused, unread): season Mar 1-Nov 30, $20-35 peak and $14 off-peak (stored $14-25 was out of date at the top), 44 sites 42-68 ft, showers/flush/dump. 50 A and water are Loop B only (14 sites); Loop A is 30 A - conflicts with rec.gov's own facility text, flagged. Weekend 2-night and holiday 3-night minimums written. Lakeview stands. PIN MOVE proposed onto Loop A.

AMPERAGE / WATER CONFLICT inside rec.gov: the facility text says '39 of the sites are 50-amp with water, and 5 sites are primitive', but the per-site records give 50 A and a water hookup only on the 14 Loop B sites; the 25 electric Loop A sites read 'Electricity Hookup: 30' with no water value, and the rate table prices Loop B separately ($35 against $30), which fits the per-site reading. hookups written as 50 A / water because Loop B has both (same values as stored), but most electric sites here are 30 A without a water hookup - said in the note and fee note. The USACE pages that could settle it are unread (403).

WATERFRONT (stored lakeview; no change): counted on the 0.33 m/px leaf-off frames with site coordinates plotted. Loop A is under continuous timber on a peninsula. The closest pads are A14 and A13 at the west turnaround, about 45 m and 55 m from the north shore, and A15-A17, about 25-30 m inside the tree line with an open, bare point beyond and the water roughly 100 m off at the pool in the image; all are through standing timber, none on an open apron. Loop B is 200 m+ from any shore in woods beside the park's sewage lagoons. On an open apron within 50 m: none. Lakeview is supportable for the west end of Loop A only, through leaf-off timber; if the owner wants the strict reading (a view through leaf-off timber is not a view) this goes down to not waterfront.
